features.title: OKLCH-native design token package
acceptance: design-system.manifest.json compiles to CSS custom properties, TypeScript, React Native styles and a Tailwind v4 theme

Every status token pairs with an icon token; a status expressible only as colour cannot be constructed

features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: the manifest compiles to four targets (CSS custom properties with an @supports OKLCh upgrade, TypeScript constants, React Native styles, a Tailwind v4 theme), every output committed and BYTE-COMPARED by its tests; gate 9 (contrast) ACTIVE and BLOCKING after being watched fail on five real defects, with an eight-case mutation proof in CI (scripts/verify-contrast-proof.mjs) asserting the baseline green in each — seven that must go red, and one that must stay green (a placeholder manifest status with a real failure present, proving the report-only switch); the cvdPairs assertion in gate 10; the status/icon/text triple as a TYPE, so a colour-only status fails typecheck rather than review. THREE DEFECTS FOUND IN THE APPROVED MANIFEST: (1) 37 of 38 opaque tokens had an srgb hex that did not match their own oklch, up to 6.09 dE00 — settled by ADR-0043, srgb is now engine-derived and a hand-edited hex fails the gate; (2) a DUPLICATE JSON KEY meant the top-level "status": "approved" never survived parsing, so gate.contrast.blockingWhenStatus compared against an object and the gate could never block — the pairing block is renamed statusPairing; (3) five WCAG AA failures and five CVD separation failures in the approved values, corrected in ADR-0044, whose real content is the decision to classify status.* as usage:"text" (4.5:1) rather than nonText (3:1). NOT DELIVERED: the half of gate 9 that scans RENDERED surfaces for colour-only status indicators — no component exists until F-017, and the gate prints that on every run. THE COLOUR-SCIENCE REVIEW RETURNED CHANGES REQUIRED AND FOUND FOUR REAL DEFECTS IN THE GATE, ALL FIXED: (a) the comment justifying a single severity check was FALSE — Machado is not monotone, and light status.warn/status.bad under tritan scores 61.2 at severity 0.90 against 65.8 at 1.0, so all eleven tabulated severities are now checked; (b) the separation claim was model-dependent — under Vienot total dichromacy, which color-engine.md assigns to exactly this case, light status.ok/status.warn under protan scored 59.6, BELOW the declared 60, so both models are now checked and the worse taken, and the values moved again to clear it; (c) the alpha-compositing comment was factually INVERTED — for a light overlay on a dark ground the linear reading is 2.2x more PERMISSIVE, not stricter, and the encoded model is what browsers and React Native actually draw, so both are now computed and the worse taken; (d) gate coverage was driven entirely by pairsWith, so nine tokens per theme were checked by nothing while looking exactly like tokens that passed — a token covered by nothing now fails unless it declares an uncheckedReason. ALSO CORRECTED: a wrong unit in ADR-0044 (11/255 is the encoded byte, not the linear value), the chromaCeiling field name (surfaceAndText, when the rule had become universal, was an invitation to re-derive the exemption-by-classification bug from the field name), a missing Lab-illuminant statement on ADR-0043 dE00 column, and a factually wrong comment in packages/cvd-engine/src/machado.ts claiming every reference implementation applies the matrices in encoded sRGB — R colorspace and DaltonLens apply them in linear. The palette was recomputed under BOTH conventions and clears the minimum either way (61.9 linear, 64.0 encoded), which is now recorded there. INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED on the third evaluator attempt (the first two died on session limits). The evaluation reproduced every gate green and returned FAIL on the RECORD, which no gate reads: ADR-0044 value table showed the intermediate correction rather than what shipped, and DESIGN-SYSTEM.md claimed a TypeScript brand that no code applied — TextToken/LargeTextToken were phantom brands nothing produced. Both fixed; the types are now literal unions DERIVED from the manifest usage field. It also found that NOTHING isolated checkContrast: the one contrast mutation also broke the derived-hex check, so a checkContrast returning passes:true unconditionally left gate 9 exiting 0 and all eight mutations green — verified by neutering it. Now covered by test/check.test.ts and a ninth proof case. Also fixed: turbo.json gave test:contrast no dependency on its own build; the severity-sweep decoy matched rows scoring 100 at every severity; and six stale measurements including the record of a re-measurement that was not itself re-measured. NOT REVIEWED BY A HUMAN: the corrected palette was reviewed by the designer and colour-scientist subagents, not by the person who approved it; the manifest carries a valuesChangedSinceApproval field saying so, because status:approved is the one field a gate reads. All colour maths is delegated to @irodora/color-difference and @irodora/cvd-engine, so nothing here re-implements a metric. FOUND AND RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED: F-067 (the two themes assert opposite salience hierarchies — pre-existing), F-068 (swatch edge against an arbitrary sample), F-069 (status colour adjacent to a sample). border.strong composited over a light surface reaches 1.17:1; it is in no pairsWith so nothing checks it, and that is recorded rather than silently widened.

features.title: CVD engine and separation scoring
acceptance: Brettel-Vienot dichromacy and Machado anomalous trichromacy at severity 0 to 1
Dichromat simulation of a published confusion-line pair yields DeltaE00 below 2
One separation score in [0,100], combining post-simulation DeltaE00 with lightness difference, used identically by the UI and the recommendation engine
Gate 10 (cvd) activates
features.notes: IN PROGRESS. DELIVERED: Machado anomalous trichromacy for all three deficiencies across CONTINUOUS severity (culori snaps to 0.1 steps because its interpolation weight is Math.round(t % 0.1), always 0 — we interpolate, and the oracle is consulted only at the 11 tabulated points); Vienot dichromacy for protan and deutan; one separation score in [0,100] (E-005); gate 10 ACTIVE after being watched fail. NOT DELIVERED — acceptance criterion 1 is only partly met: TRITAN DICHROMACY. Vienot's single-plane simplification is not accurate for tritanopia, whose two half-planes diverge, so simulateDichromacy THROWS for it rather than returning a plausible wrong answer that would feed the separation score. The full two-half-plane Brettel 1997 construction is the remaining work, and there is no oracle for it in either library — the check will have to be the confusion-line property, as it is for the other two. THE BLOCKER IS IDENTIFIED AND PINNED: XYZ_TO_LMS_HPE is the WRONG fundamental set. A copunctal point is the chromaticity of the missing cone fundamental, so it is derivable from the LMS-to-XYZ columns; HPE gives tritan (0.1680, 0.0000) against the published (0.171, -0.003) — agreement to 0.003 — but protan (0.8374, 0.1626) against (0.747, 0.253) and deutan (2.3019, -1.3019) against (1.400, -0.400). The published points are Smith-Pokorny, which is also what Vienot derived from, so the remaining construction needs Smith-Pokorny fundamentals plus the four anchor stimuli (475/575 nm for protan and deutan, 485/660 nm for tritan). The fundamental set is now SETTLED: Smith-Pokorny reproduces all three published copunctal points (protan 0.0007, deutan 0.0002, tritan 0.0048). The ANCHOR STIMULI are the blocker, and an attempt was refuted rather than shipped: recalled anchors disagree with Vienot — which is the published single-plane reduction of Brettel, so a real oracle — by 32.5 dE00 (protan) and 57.4 (deutan), and the diagnostic explains why: the two half-plane normals sit 88.4 degrees apart where Vienot validity requires ~0. They cannot be derived here — computing LMS at a wavelength needs CIE colour-matching functions and there is NO spectral data in the dependency tree and no Brettel implementation to check against. FINISHING THIS NEEDS A DECISION, NOT CODE: vendor CIE colour-matching functions (a content and licensing question per content/AGENTS.md), obtain a trustworthy transcription of Brettel published anchor table, or attest criterion 1 under ADR-0038. Criterion 2 is met for protan and deutan using the kernel of the published Vienot matrix; note that pairs built from the classic published COPUNCTAL POINTS only collapse to ~5.2 dE00, because those points and Vienot's matrices come from different cone fundamentals. Recorded as a golden entry.

attested.criterion: Brettel-Vienot dichromacy and Machado anomalous trichromacy at severity 0 to 1
attested.verifiedBy: TRITAN DICHROMACY ONLY. Everything else in this criterion is gated: Machado anomalous trichromacy for all three deficiencies across continuous severity, and Vienot dichromacy for protan and deutan, are covered by gate 5 and gate 10 (ADR-0038 section 4 — where a part is checkable, that part stays gated). Tritan dichromacy needs the two-half-plane Brettel 1997 construction, which needs the LMS anchor stimuli at 485 and 660 nm. Those cannot be derived or verified here: computing LMS at a wavelength requires CIE colour-matching functions, there is no spectral data in the repository or its dependency tree, and neither culori nor colorjs.io implements Brettel. An attempt using recalled anchors was REFUTED and not shipped — it disagreed with Vienot (the published single-plane reduction of Brettel, and therefore a real oracle for protan and deutan) by 32.5 dE00 protan and 57.4 deutan, and the diagnostic showed the half-plane normals 88.4 degrees apart where Vienot validity requires ~0. DISCHARGED BY: implementing the construction against either vendored CIE colour-matching functions or a trustworthy transcription of Brettel published anchor table, and accepting only if BOTH checks pass — agreement with Vienot on protan and deutan, and near-coplanar half-plane normals. NOTE ON THE BAR: ADR-0038 asks for "verifying it requires a system we do not control". This is missing published source data rather than a missing system, which is a weaker case than a VPS or a physical device — recorded plainly rather than glossed. What makes it defensible is that tritan CVD is NOT unsupported: Machado tritanomaly is delivered across full severity and the separation score covers all three deficiencies through the Machado path, so only tritan DICHROMACY specifically is owed.

features.title: Gamut mapping
acceptance: Out-of-gamut colours map by OKLCh chroma reduction, preserving lightness and hue within stated bounds
Mapping an in-gamut colour is idempotent, asserted by property test
Golden set of known out-of-gamut colours and their mapped results
features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: gamutMap and gamutMapDetail in @irodora/color-spaces — OKLCh chroma bisection, 32 halvings, holding L and H, for sRGB and Display-P3. Zero new colour maths: every number is an existing engine conversion, and the feature is a search over a predicate. THE DECISION IS ADR-0045 AND IT IS A DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM CSS COLOR 4. The standard adds a MINDE early stop that returns the CLIPPED colour once it is within a JND in dEok, and dEok tolerates hue movement — measured against colorjs.io toGamut({method:css}) over 30 out-of-gamut colours, CSS drifts hue up to 11.97 degrees where we drift 2.6e-5, and the two results differ by up to 5.21 dE00. Our implementation was cross-checked against culori clampChroma, an independent implementation of the SAME algorithm: agreement 0.0063 dE00. The MINDE step was also structurally unavailable — dEok lives in @irodora/color-difference, which depends on this package, so implementing it would have meant a second implementation of a shipped function. Both reasons are recorded; the measurement is the one that decided it. THE STATED BOUND, which acceptance criterion 1 asks for: L and H are preserved EXACTLY in OKLCh (7e-12, the round-trip noise). After rendering, a final clamp of at most GAMUT_EPSILON=1e-7 per channel applies, and near the black point that tiny absolute movement is a large relative one — hue drift reaches 23 degrees below result L,C=0.01 where OKLCh hue is not a meaningful angle, and is 6.9e-5 degrees above L,C=0.05. Tabulated in the test rather than asserted at one convenient cutoff. THREE CASES ARE NOT CHROMA REDUCTION and each is an explicit branch: already in gamut (the early return is what makes idempotence exact), achromatic, and out of gamut in LIGHTNESS where no chroma fits and lightnessOutOfRange says so rather than a loop returning whatever it last held. THE DECOY is per-channel clipping — the algorithm almost everything else uses — implemented in the test and measured at 33.6 degrees of hue shift, with our own drift asserted beside it as the baseline. FOUND AND RECORDED, NOT FIXED: F-071, two pre-existing flaky property tests. oklab.test.ts round-trips 5000 unseeded fast-check samples against a 1e-12 bound and failed once during this feature at 1.2477e-12 before passing six consecutive full-suite runs; the F-003 evaluation found a second in packages/testing. A blocking gate that can go red for a reason unrelated to the change teaches people to re-run until green.

features.title: The Color value type and reproducibility envelope
acceptance: Color carries required Provenance; an unclassified colour is not constructible
Provenance records source, confidence, conditions and originSpace

features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: the Color value type (canonical XYZ + required Provenance), fromXyz / fromSpace / unsafeFromHex / withProvenance, CaptureConditions, and the ReproducibilityEnvelope with a canonical serialisation and a historical replay fixture. No colour maths: this package is a facade and every conversion is @irodora/color-spaces. THE DESIGN DECISION: Provenance is a DISCRIMINATED UNION on source, not an interface with an optional conditions field. ADR-0005 says conditions is required when the source is estimated or calibrated, and an optional field only asks nicely — an estimate that lost its capture conditions would still compile, which is exactly the object nobody should be able to build. CaptureConditions was NOT invented for this: its fields are specified in docs/architecture/color-engine.md and match FR-17 (illuminant) and FR-18 (quality) exactly, so the union requires real data rather than an empty object. THE UNION BROKE THE WIRE PIN, AND THAT IS THE MECHANISM WORKING. ADR-0036 pins the engine type to the Zod schema at compile time; adding conditions turned it red immediately, which forced the contract to move in the same commit. But the union then WEAKENED the pin in a way that passed silently: keyof on a union returns only the keys COMMON to every member, so an optional field added to one member type-checked cleanly. Verified by doing it. The pin is now asserted PER MEMBER, and scripts/verify-contract-pin.mjs proves it — four probes, each adding an optional field to a different part of the schema, each asserted to turn typecheck red with the baseline asserted green first. EVERY CALL SITE IS REVIEWED, MADE COUNTABLE: scripts/verify-unsafe-call-sites.mjs enumerates unsafeFromHex call sites and runs inside pnpm lint; a new one fails the build until someone adds it to the reviewed list, which is the moment the review happens. It is a script rather than a test because the colour-engine ESLint zone forbids node: imports even in tests (NFR-3), and the alternative was weakening the strictest guard in the repository. THE REPLAY FIXTURE PINS HISTORICAL VERSIONS, not current ones, and asserts it: a fixture written from todays CORE_VERSION compares the code to itself and goes green for free. That assertion caught one of my own entries using 0.1.0.

features.title: Cross-theme salience hierarchy for the status tokens, and the APCA floor for dark error
acceptance: The salience rank of status.ok, status.warn and status.bad against each theme own ground is the same in both themes
Every status token meets the APCA Lc 45 large-text floor against every surface it is declared on, or its restriction is recorded as a machine-checkable field
The chosen rank is recorded with its reason, not inferred from the values
The contrast gate asserts the rank, so it cannot drift back
features.notes: FOUND BY THE F-003 DESIGN AND COLOUR-SCIENCE REVIEWS. PRE-EXISTING — not introduced by F-003. TWO DRIVERS, ONE DECISION. (1) SALIENCE INVERSION: measured against each theme own background, the dark theme says caution is the loudest state and error the quietest, while the light theme says error is loudest by nearly 2x. A user toggling the theme gets an inverted status hierarchy. The cause is that the approved system holds the rank of OKLCh L constant across two grounds of OPPOSITE polarity, and L rank does not survive that flip — the invariant that makes the themes one system is rank of CONTRAST against own ground. (2) THE APCA FLOOR: dark.status.bad sits at APCA Lc -37.5 to -38.6 against its three declared surfaces — below the Lc 45 LARGE-text floor of 0.98G-4g — while WCAG reads 4.92 to 5.58 and passes. ADR-0044 classifies status.* as usage:text precisely because the product tints the label, so this is body copy below even the large-text floor in the DEFAULT theme. MEASURED AND INFEASIBLE SEPARATELY: holding status.ok and status.warn at their current values, NO value of status.bad reaches even Lc 40 while keeping CVD separation at or above 60 — the APCA floor and the separation minimum are in direct tension at the current lightness arrangement. A jointly feasible solution exists and was computed during F-003 — dark ok L0.67 C0.12 H158, warn L0.70 C0.14 H70, bad L0.82 C0.10 H18, worst separation 63.1, every token above Lc 45 — but it makes error the LIGHTEST token in the dark theme, which is exactly the salience re-arrangement in driver (1). That is a redesign larger than either defect and belongs to a person rather than to a gate-building task. Until it is decided, gate 9 prints the three pairings in a separate RED band on every run so they cannot be mistaken for the ordinary WCAG/APCA disagreements.

features.title: Swatch edge treatment against an arbitrary sample
acceptance: A sample of ANY colour has a perceptible edge against the swatch.well beneath it
The treatment is verified against the worst-case sample, not a convenient one

features.notes: FOUND BY THE F-003 DESIGN REVIEW. swatch.hairline claimed its edge was perceptible against ANY value; a single-tone 16 percent white inset cannot deliver that against a light sample, by construction, and no fixed-token check can cover an arbitrary garment colour. The claim was softened in F-003 (golden rule 11 applies to the design system own claims) and the treatment that WOULD deliver it — a two-tone inset, or an inset ring plus an outer rule against the well — needs components. ALSO HERE: the review asks that a real dark garment colour be put on the corrected swatch.well (#2B2A28 dark, which is darker than the #383533 the design review saw, because the hex was the defect ADR-0043 fixed) and looked at. A navy or charcoal sample on that well is near 1:1 in luminance and the hairline becomes the only edge cue.

features.title: Status colour may not sit beside a colour sample

features.notes: FOUND BY THE F-003 DESIGN REVIEW. Nothing in the manifest stops a saturated status colour sitting next to a sample, and simultaneous contrast means it pushes that sample the opposite way — a deep red beside a swatch makes the swatch read green. The Lens result is exactly where a low-confidence bad indicator wants to live, beside the colour. The swatch.well separator is already mandatory for decorative colour; this extends the same rule to the semantic tokens and makes it checkable.

features.title: border.strong meets 3:1 as an outlined control boundary
acceptance: border.strong reaches 3:1 against every surface it can sit on, under BOTH the linear and the encoded compositing model
It is declared in pairsWith rather than carrying an uncheckedReason, so the gate checks it
The design rule that a border is never a solid grey is either met or deliberately amended
features.notes: FOUND BY THE F-003 COLOUR-SCIENCE REVIEW. border.strong role is Outlined controls, which is a UI component boundary under WCAG 1.4.11 and therefore owes 3:1 — it is not the decorative-hairline exemption that covers border. MEASURED over its own declared grounds: dark 3.11:1 linear (worst ground surface.3) but only 1.41:1 encoded (over background); light 1.17:1 linear and 1.41:1 encoded (over surface.3). It fails under the encoded model in both themes, and the encoded model is what a browser and React Native actually draw. THE CONFLICT: reaching 3:1 needs roughly 53 percent alpha, which is a solid grey line, and the design system states a border is a translucent overlay and NEVER a solid grey because depth must read as lift rather than outline. So this is a design decision, not a value tweak — either the outline stops being the only thing identifying the control (a filled or tinted control state would remove the 1.4.11 obligation), or the never-a-solid-grey rule is amended. F-003 made the token VISIBLE rather than fixing it: it carries an uncheckedReason with these ratios in it, and the gate now fails any token that is covered by nothing and does not declare why.

features.title: The property-test gates are deterministic
acceptance: Every fast-check property runs from a recorded seed, so a failure is reproducible and a pass is not luck
No gate can go red for a reason unrelated to the change under test
A test whose tolerance is within a small factor of the true error bound states the measured margin
features.notes: TWO FLAKES OBSERVED, both pre-existing and neither caused by the feature that hit them. (1) packages/color-spaces test/oklab.test.ts "round-trips arbitrary OKLab values" uses fc.assert with 5000 runs and NO seed, asserting max round-trip error below 1e-12. It failed once during F-009 at 1.2477e-12 — a 25 percent overshoot, so it will recur — and then passed six consecutive full-suite runs. An unseeded generator means the gate samples a different region every run, so a red is not reproducible and a green is not evidence. (2) FOUND BY THE F-003 EVALUATION: packages/testing createPrng "stays inside [0, 1)" timed out at 5000 ms under the 37-task parallel turbo run and passes in 1.8 s in isolation — a 100k-iteration loop on the default vitest timeout. THE POINT IS NOT TIDINESS: gate 4 and gate 5 are blocking, and a blocking gate that can go red for a reason unrelated to the change teaches people to re-run it until it is green, which is how a real regression gets waved through. The fix for (1) is a recorded seed plus a stated margin between the tolerance and the measured worst case; for (2) an explicit timeout or a smaller loop.
